lifecycle: Clock: t = server time now - the occurrence's publishedAt (an event) or the phase's startedAt (a stage). Never a local start time, never an animation's end. The server's endsAt and expiresAt are unchanged by any presentation.

Late load or reconnect: if t >= the film's end, draw the final state at once (no replay); if 0 <= t < end, seek to t; a stage presentation (capsule, vote result) snaps to its current pose. Never replay a historical death, Sync or cinematic.

Duplicates: key every presentation by its event id (or phase id); one id plays once per page. A repeated or older viewRevision draws nothing new. An event past expiresAt (publishedAt + 30 s) never starts.

Cancellation: a newer viewRevision that changes what a presentation shows (a seat moved, a phase ended) cancels it: remove its nodes and draw the latest authoritative state. Cancelling never changes game state.

Precedence: terminal result > Sync > Captain commands > medical outcome (death before rescue at one berth) > attack, Blackout and blocked > movement and placement > ambient idles. A higher presentation starting in the same region cancels a lower one to its final state; different regions (another room panel) play concurrently.
Hidden tab: pause nothing on the server; on return compute t again from the server clock and seek or snap. Audio never plays in a hidden tab.

Interaction: press areas, name tags, room labels, timers, Pass and navigation never move, scale or hide for a film; a film may darken or shake only the art layer. Pointer events pass through every film layer.

Gameplay visibility (the owner's review of 6 November 2026): by default every film is a board treatment, on phones and the display alike: drawn in the board's own layers (a room's art, the board's film band), under the press areas, slot hits, room labels, timers, Pass and bars, so it covers nothing a player selects or reads. A presentation that covers the board (a display cut, a comic page) plays only in a phase where nobody decides (HACK_RESULT, VOTE_RESULT, FINISHED, ABORTED; design/cinematic/lib/visibility.mjs) and inside that phase's own time; in any other phase it gives way to its board treatment from its first frame. No film waits for, extends or takes time from a phase. One film has a stage of its own (owner decision P27, 6 November 2026): after an actual Blackhole Sync, a separate six-second presentation stage, then the full 60-second Jail vote; only the Blackhole's stage cut plays there (its phase kind is R16; until a view carries it, the board treatment plays at the Jail vote's start). No other stage exists: in particular no covering EJECT stage is approved, so the EJECT's display cut is a review study that nothing mounts (design/cinematic/lib/visibility.mjs PRESENTATION_STAGES, NO_RUNTIME_COVER).

Reduced motion: honoured at load and when changed during playback (a change mid-film switches to the reduced variant at the same t). Reduced variants carry the same information with fades of 80-120 ms, no travel, camera, shake, flash, particles or spin.
Audio: public events only, from the cue sheet (never only inside a video); muted by the device setting; private, room-filtered and pair-private presentations play no public audio by default.
Asset failure: a missing picture or video never blocks: the scene's static final state (or its words in the live region) stands alone.

requests.ask: Answered by the owner (P27, 6 November 2026): "after actual Blackhole Sync, there is a separate six-second presentation stage. The full 60-second Jail vote starts afterward." The display plays the 5.2 s stage cut in that stage (it ends 0.8 s before the vote, and takes nothing from it); phones play the board treatment, behind the crew, from the stage's start; reduced motion plays the still blackhole on every surface. The stage's phase kind is R16. Until a view carries it, the Blackhole plays its board treatment at the Jail vote's start, covering nothing (the safe fallback).

Answered by the owner's review of 6 November 2026: the capsule's exit stays the live game's, on the board. S2's approved exit plays on every surface, the display included; there is no exit page. Nothing more is needed.

Answered by the owner's review of 6 November 2026: the Rescue ends on the authoritative game state. A healed patient who is free returns to Room A or B; one still detained returns to the Jail, wherever the published snapshot places them. The film follows that placement: the patient walks out of the ward, the berth is left empty, and their playable figure at its place is never hidden. RESCUED and the snapshot carry all of it; nothing more is needed.

MOVEMENT_COMPLETED and PLACEMENT_CHANGED carry seatIds, location and slotId but not the origin slot: a walk needs the previous finalized placement (the client keeps the last snapshot). Confirm that a reconnecting client without the previous snapshot snaps instead of walking.

Neutral shared transit: navigation.lastMovedRound and arrivedAt are public; a neutral "the ship moved" presentation needs nothing else. The office-private route view (privateNavigation) needs the previous position to animate a step; confirm it may be derived from the previous view.

Each Promise is evaluated at its own opportunity, not at one shared moment (owner decisions P04, P23 and P24): a meeting Promise when its round's voting begins after Sync (the synced places); a Jail Vote or No Jail Vote when its round's Jail vote closes (the actual ballot, not the outcome or the admission); Captain Support when the specified election closes (every ballot in which the recipient is a candidate, runoffs included); Officer Selection at that election and its Officer appointment. Same-round Promises finalize at the close of their opportunity in that round; only election Promises may stay Pending until their election or the match end. Confirm that each promises[].status change (Pending to Fulfilled / Not fulfilled / Condition not met) arrives with the viewRevision that closes its own opportunity, so its result plays once, then, and never from a speculative state.
A shown drawing's arrival: windows[].drawings[] has order and round but no publishedAt; a stamp-in needs the moment it was shown, or the client stamps on first sight only (no replay on reconnect).

P14 gives the Engineer a private confirmation of the fixed identities, but the player view has only abilities.engineerSpent. Add the Engineer's own record, e.g. abilities.engineerCapture { round, seatIds } (Engineer only), so the confirmation shows the identities the server fixed at registration, never the client's preview (someone may move between the two). Until then the file says only that the capture was used.

abilities.shipHackSpent cannot tell a hack registered this round (still to apply at this round's navigation) from one used in an earlier round. Add abilities.shipHackRound (Hacker only) so the file can say "applies at this round's navigation" or "used in Round N". Until then a spent hack is drawn as used, its round unnamed.

Answered by the owner (P28, 6 November 2026): "from Round 2, every navigation opportunity has the same full 15-second route-setting window. Only the eligible Officer receives controls for a genuine tie. Early selection cannot shorten the window. Public wording, animation, sound and timing must not reveal whether a tie occurred." The candidate's NAV_TIE phase (15 s) then runs at every opportunity, so its kind and timing say nothing; the public strip and the Captain's panel already read the same in every navigation stage, read no offer or choice, and nothing public moves or sounds on the Officer's choice. The name NAV_TIE no longer means a tie; Backend may rename the phase, and the design follows the name it publishes.

privateNavigation.tieChoice and .confirmation have no settled meaning (a tie to choose now, or one chosen; the acknowledgement awaited, or one given). The office panel reads the stage from phase.kind, the controls from offers, and "acknowledged" only from the client's own accepted receipt, so an office that reconnects after acknowledging sees "your acknowledgement is closed". Ask: define them, for example confirmation as the acknowledgements already given, so a reconnect can say "you acknowledged".

The patient's console cannot show its own result. An accepted PANEL_CODE is only REGISTERED, and abilities.panelAttemptSpent turns true for a right and a wrong number alike, so the view never says whether a shared injection was reserved, whether the Rescue stage treated the patient or spent it without effect, or whether the Blackhole's Sync did not keep the request; and no rejection code says that no injection was available (P21: the request is refused before the number is checked, and nothing is spent). The brief asks for pending-reservation, wrong, exhausted and no-effect feedback. Ask: the patient's own record, e.g. abilities.panelRequest { round, result: RESERVED | WRONG, status: QUEUED | TREATED | NO_EFFECT | DISCARDED } (that patient only, never the Doctor's count), and a rejection code NO_INJECTION that is the same whatever number was sent, so an empty inventory never confirms the Doctor's number. If the owner prefers the patient not to learn the result before the Rescue stage, the server sends no result and the console keeps "registered"; it never guesses. Until then the console says only "Your number is registered. Your one attempt is used." and a refusal says "Nothing was used".

A Promise card must state its exact terms (brief; motion requirements), but three terms and one field have no stated sense. (a) NO_JAIL_VOTE has no target (the contract allows one only on JAIL_VOTE): does it rule out voting to jail the recipient, or any Jail ballot at all? The cards read it as "not against the recipient". (b) Answered by the owner (6 November 2026): a meeting Promise is the giver's place alone, as the cards read ("Your giver-only 'Meet in A/B' Promise wording is correct. Keep it"). (c) electionId is an opaque identifier: add the election's round (e.g. electionRound) so a card can say "Round 5's Captain election", not only "the next Captain election". (d) promiseQuota.given and .received: does true mean the lifetime slot is used, or still open? Until defined, the ledger reads the slots from the accepted records and never reads promiseQuota.

The lobby's join states need three answers from planet-service.ts. (a) What can a requester read while its admission is pending: a session snapshot with selfSeatId null, a refusal until approved, or nothing? The lobby draws "the host has your request" from requestAdmission's ok answer alone, and treats a snapshot with selfSeatId null as the same state. (b) No operation declines an admission: does a request the host never approves stay pending until setup begins, and what does the requester then receive? Until answered, the requester waits with the room code shown and no countdown. (c) A display has no seat, so an admitted display and a pending one both read selfSeatId null: add the requester's own standing (e.g. self: { kind, admitted }) or confirm that the client's remembered kind decides.

A recipient-private marker for the Round 3 Supply delivery. self.ordinaryWeapons cannot say why it grew: an actual Blackhole Sync also restores weapons spent in a discarded reality (P03), and the owner's correction of 6 November 2026 says "Restored weapons after Blackhole Sync must not be presented as a new Supply delivery." Ask: a player-audience PlanetEvent kind SUPPLY_RECEIVED (audience the recipient, seatIds [recipient], actorSeatId null, round 3, published with the Supply stage's view revision), or an equivalent own-view field. Until it exists, no delivery is drawn: the count changes at rest ("Ordinary weapons: 1."), never "received".

P27's presentation stage needs a phase kind in the view (proposed BLACKHOLE_PRESENTATION, 6000 ms, between the actual Sync's BLACKHOLE_SYNCED and JAIL_VOTE), so a client can tell the stage from the vote and play the covering stage cut only there. The protocol 3 candidate has none. Until a view carries it (Frontend passes Backend's name to presentationIn()), the Blackhole plays its board treatment at the Jail vote's start.

scenes.audience: pair-private (the giver's and the recipient's own phones only)
scenes.trigger: offers OFFER_PROMISE (targetSeatIds, promiseTargetSeatIds), ACCEPT_PROMISE, DECLINE_PROMISE during private talk (phase HACK); promises[] (offerStatus, status) and the command receipts

beats.start: six cards in private talk; the exact terms reviewed before sending
beats.loop: the offer in transit; Accept and Decline of equal weight
beats.exit: the Pending seal on acceptance; the result's seal as that Promise's own opportunity closes (R6)

durations.full: offer 720 ms, arrive 760 ms, accept 560 ms, decline 600 ms, result 720 ms

scenes.final: the ledger: one Promise given and one received, each with its status
scenes.cancel: phase end (an unanswered offer expires); a refused command changes nothing; a reconnect draws everything at rest
scenes.audio: none (pair-private: a sound would tell the table that a Promise was offered, made or decided)
scenes.concurrency: one accepted Promise given and one received per match; declined and unanswered offers use nothing
assets: design/library/promises/ (six kind pictures, four result seals, the envelope, the card band and the tray mark; state maps, words, motion)

scenes.audience: window-scoped (players at either end of a window); the pad station-private; the station markers public on the board
scenes.trigger: windows[] (windowId, canDraw, drawings[] by order); offers SHOW_WINDOW (windowIds); the SHOW_WINDOW receipt; phase BLACKOUT with blackout.previewEndsAt

beats.start: the window to the other room: its lintel, the pane with this round's shown drawings
beats.loop: the local pad at a station (inks, widths, undo, clear); Show after a warning that nothing can be erased
beats.exit: the drawing lifts into the pane, SHOWN; a new drawing drops in on first sight; the panes stay lit through the Blackout's first five seconds, the shade lowers at its authoritative preview deadline (blackout.previewEndsAt; dark from the Blackout's start if the deadline is missing) and rises when it ends

durations.full: show 760 ms, arrive 420 ms, dark 420 ms, light 320 ms

scenes.final: the pane with every drawing shown this round, numbered, with its author; empty at the next round
scenes.cancel: round end expires the drawings; a refused Show keeps the local drawing; a reconnect draws everything at rest
scenes.precedence: window audience only; the Blackout darkens every window from its preview deadline
scenes.audio: none (a sound would tell the table that someone drew or showed)
scenes.concurrency: append-only, in shown order; any number per round within the drawing budget
assets: design/library/windows/ (three lintels, the station marker, the pad paper, the Blackout shade, the tray mark; the drawing renderer; state maps, words, motion)

scenes.status: library group 7 (proposal) over the arrival films (group 2)
scenes.audience: public (endReveal on FINISHED); each screen's own connection and failure states
scenes.trigger: phase FINISHED / ABORTED; result {winner, reason, alienCoWinner}; endReveal {roles, code}; the client's own transport and clock

beats.start: the arrival film (group 2)
beats.loop: the reveal: the side's banner and emblem, each role turning face up in seat order, the Code stamping into its plate; or the no-survivors flat line; or the abort
beats.exit: held: the end screen at rest

durations.full: arrival 3400 ms phone / 4200 ms display, then the reveal 1940 ms (7 seats) to 2120 ms (9); no survivors 1300 ms

scenes.final: the end screen: the ending in words, every role by side, winners marked from the result, the Code
scenes.cancel: none; a late join seeks, a reconnect after the end draws it at rest (filmDecision)
scenes.audio: the arrival's single sting (public), no new cue; the reveal, the abort and recovery are silent
scenes.rosters: 7, 8 and 9: the reveal lists every seat
